## Zoning Analysis: 1256 N Artesian Ave, Chicago IL
**PIN:** 16012280180000 | **Parcel Resolution:** Authoritative

> **Note:** This parcel is currently flagged as **city-owned** (status: "Owned by City" / "Interest"). Any development project will require acquiring or controlling the parcel from the City of Chicago first.

---

### 1. Zoning District in Effect

This parcel is zoned **RM-4.5** (Residential Multi-Unit). The district was established by ordinance A7210, dated September 5, 2007; the zoning map record was last updated October 27, 2021. The parcel has **not been recently rezoned**. Verify on the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning). *Code authority:* [1] (§17-2-0104, current through the Council Journal of March 18, 2026; a later amendment may not be reflected).

---

### 2. Is a 3+ Unit Residential Building Permitted by Right?

**Yes.** RM-4.5 expressly permits multi-unit residential buildings [1]. Three or more units are a by-right use in this district — no special use approval or Planned Development is required (the parcel is not in a Planned Development). The binding constraint is density, addressed in Part 6 below.

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

All figures are from the RM-4.5 zoning table [1]:

| Standard | RM-4.5 Value |
|---|---|
| **FAR** | 1.7 |
| **Max Height** | 45–47 ft (varies by lot frontage) |
| **Min Lot Area per Dwelling Unit** | 700 sq ft |
| **Min Lot Size** | 1,650 sq ft |
| **Side Setbacks** | No side setbacks required in RM districts unless abutting an R-zoned lot [4] |

Efficiency and SRO units count at smaller lot-area fractions than a standard dwelling unit — see the density table in [1] for those figures. Other factors (parking, unit sizes, lot configuration) can further constrain what is actually achievable [1].

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

- **Special District** — This parcel falls within a Special District designation. No specific ordinance was returned in the data, so the exact restrictions are not confirmed here; verify with the Department of Planning and Development.
- **ADU-Eligible Area** — The parcel is in an Additional Dwelling Unit–Allowed RS Area [2] (§17-7-0570). Note: ADU rules in [2] target RS single-family zones; their applicability to an RM-4.5 parcel should be confirmed with the Department of Housing (§17-7-0572).
- **ARO Zone** — Subject to the Affordable Requirements Ordinance. Residential projects meeting the ARO threshold must provide affordable units or pay an in-lieu fee. West Town has 20 ARO projects totaling 291 affordable units in the community area.
- **No Planned Development, landmark/historic district, lakefront protection, or PMD** applies.
- **Not transit-oriented development (TOD) eligible** — no TOD parking reduction is available under the Connected Communities Ordinance.
- **Flood Zone X** — Area of Minimal Flood Hazard; not a Special Flood Hazard Area; flood insurance is not typically required.
- **No TIF, Opportunity Zone, or Enterprise Zone** applies to this parcel.

*Verify overlays:* [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning) and the Department of Planning & Development.

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit-Related Reduction

For RM districts, off-street parking must be located on the same zoning lot as the dwelling units served [3] (§17-10-0602-B). The standard RM residential parking ratio applies (typically 1 space per unit — confirm the exact ratio from §17-10-0200 for RM-4.5, as the retrieved code text [5] covers D-dash districts only and does not state the RM-4.5 ratio explicitly).

**No TOD parking reduction is available** — this parcel is not TOD-eligible. The nearest CTA rail is Damen (Blue Line), 0.67 miles away — outside the threshold for a transit-served parking reduction under the Connected Communities Ordinance.

*Verify:* §17-10-0200 and §17-10-0602 [3].

---

### 6. Maximum Units by Right — Can You Build 6?

Based on the lot area per unit standard [1]:

> **3,191 sq ft ÷ 700 sq ft per unit = 4.6 → 4 units by right**

The lot supports a maximum of **4 dwelling units by right** on a lot-area basis. **6 units is not achievable by right** — it would require approximately 4,200 sq ft of lot area (6 × 700 sq ft).

**Important caveats:**
- Lot area per unit is a *floor*, not a ceiling. FAR (1.7), height (45–47 ft), and parking can all reduce this further [1].
- Efficiency or SRO units count at smaller fractions — you may be able to fit more than 4 units if some are efficiencies (confirm exact fractions from the RM-4.5 density table in §17-2-0303).
- The lot size in the county record is **3,191 sq ft** (from parcel geometry); you noted ~3,150 sq ft — either way, the yield is 4 units under the standard formula.
- To reach 6 units, you would need a rezoning to a higher-density RM district or a Planned Development.

*Verify:* §17-2-0303 [1] and the Cook County parcel record for confirmed lot area.

---

**Confidence:** High for zoning classification, FAR, height, min lot area per unit, and unit yield — all from authoritative parcel and code data. **Could not confirm:** exact RM-4.5 automobile parking ratio (code text retrieved covers D districts); specific Special District restrictions; and ADU applicability in RM-4.5. The lot area figure from parcel geometry (3,191 sq ft) should be verified against a survey.
